beats.title: World
beats.headline: Vatican City: Pope surgery OK; Bulgaria missing; Brazil polls.
beats.body:
Vatican City. Doctors at Gemelli successfully removed the lower lobe of Pope Leo XIV’s right lung in a ~90-minute video-assisted operation Tuesday afternoon; intraoperative histology confirmed lung adenocarcinoma as preoperative tests had suggested. No complications; he awoke normally, returned to the 10th-floor room, asked for dinner, and spent the evening with secretaries and Vatican staff. About one week in hospital still expected; audiences remain canceled through Oct. 20. Wednesday morning update planned on how he spent the night.

Africa. The U.S.-requested UN Security Council held closed Horn of Africa consultations Tuesday on Ethiopia–Eritrea escalation after Ethiopian forces entered Adwa; no public resolution or Council statement followed the session.

Asia. Quiet beyond this morning’s Seoul–Washington–Tokyo consults and KCNA’s “big success” claim on Monday’s tactical ballistic test; Taiwan’s overnight PLA track (five aircraft, six PLAN ships) still the latest island watch.

Europe. After this morning’s Black Sea drone hits, Bulgaria said the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 (15 crew rescued, six injured) was struck by three drones; the second ship sank with search ongoing for missing crew. Sofia summoned Russia’s ambassador and said it would deploy more unmanned maritime/air surveillance; PM sought NATO and EU support.

North America. Hurricane Simon remained a small Category 1 west of Cabo Corrientes; mainland Mexico watches were discontinued while rain and swell risk lingered for Baja and the Pacific coast. Combined flood/landslide deaths tied to Simon and former Rachel rose to at least six.

South America. Fresh runoff polls toward Oct. 25 put Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly ahead of Lula within margins of error (Datafolha ~49–45 raw; other houses near a technical tie on valid votes).

Oceania. Queensland’s Valentine Plains fire near Biloela stayed on the evening watch; South Australia’s Strathalbyn bushfire emergency was downgraded with residents still urged to monitor conditions.

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: FSD v14.3.12 wide; FAA opens Starship PEIS.
beats.body:
Tesla — FSD / Halloween OTA. Tesla pushed a wider rollout of FSD Supervised v14.3.12 with software 2026.38.5 (Halloween Mode) to HW4 and eligible HW3 Ryzen cars—pairing seasonal cabin features with a unified model stack across FSD, Actually Smart Summon, and Robotaxi. Stockholder-relevant: another fleet software wave while NHTSA’s school-zone Robotaxi petition (briefed this morning) remains open.

SpaceX — Starbase cadence paperwork. The FAA filed notice of intent to prepare a programmatic EIS on SpaceX’s request for up to 456 Starship launches and 912 landings a year from Boca Chica (comments due Nov. 30)—not approval; current authorization stays 25 launches / 50 landings. CRS-35 Dragon remains en route for Thursday docking (see NASA).

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: FAA opens PEIS for 456 Starbase Starship flights.
beats.body:
Starbase environmental review. Tuesday’s Federal Register public-inspection notice kicks off scoping for a programmatic EIS on SpaceX’s proposed leap from 25 authorized annual Starship launches at Boca Chica toward a phased ceiling of 100, then up to 456 launches (and up to 912 landings counting recoveries from elsewhere). Meetings planned mid-November in Brownsville and Port Isabel; nothing in the notice green-lights the cadence yet.

Commercial cargo. Quiet otherwise beyond CRS-35’s on-time morning launch and booster RTLS (already briefed)—Dragon still frames Thursday ~11 a.m. ET docking.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Pope lobe removed; Roche: TC stays; Acutis Friday.
beats.body:
Miami. Archdiocese weekend roundup highlights Friday’s St. Carlo Acutis Eucharistic Miracles Exposition at St. Mark (Southwest Ranches)—exhibit 5–7 p.m., keynote and Adoration 7–9 p.m., free tickets—plus Oct. 17 parish golf classic, Schott Communities 5K, and Seton craft show. Emmaus / Emaús retreats run Oct. 16–18. No new clergy assignment bulletin this evening.

Universal Church / Europe. Gemelli confirmed adenocarcinoma and a successful lower-lobe resection (see World). Separately, Cardinal Arthur Roche told Ad Vaticanum Pope Leo XIV “is not going to change Traditionis Custodes” and “is not going to go back to Summorum Pontificum,” pointing to recent papal remarks at Notre-Dame and on Sacrosanctum Concilium; Rorate and NCR-adjacent coverage amplified the line Tuesday.

United States / Latin America / other regions. Quiet on fresh episcopal appointments beyond Monday’s Yaghi (Mexico Maronite) and Santo Domingo succession already briefed this morning.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown still Oct. 3; Acutis expo Friday keynote.
beats.body:
Countdown to the Kingdom. Rechecked this evening: nothing newer than Oct. 3—Marija’s “Time of Prayer for Peace,” Elizabeth Kindelmann (“Satan Will be Blinded”), and Pedro Regis (“Humanity is Sick”).

Latest Marian message. Our Lady’s Sept. 25 Medjugorje message through Marija remains the newest monthly message (October’s 25th not out yet)—families renewing the Rosary for peace so she may intercede before the Most High.

Eucharistic signs / missions. Miami’s Acutis exposition continues with Friday’s keynote and Adoration night (see Catholic / Miami). No sober new chip or digital-ID headline tonight worth elevating.

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Heat host Nets tomorrow; Galactic Racer still buzzing.
beats.body: Heat bring the preseason home tomorrow vs. Brooklyn at Kaseya Center (7:30 p.m. ET), then close the exhibition at Orlando Oct. 16. On the Star Wars side, Galactic Racer (PS5, Xbox, PC; free for Prime on Luna) is still the week’s bright arcade hit more than a week after launch—Sebulba, Crait, and the chaotic podracing loop remain the easy smile before bed—while Lucasfilm’s Ahsoka Season 2 still aims at January 20, 2027.
